questions.stem: Let J(w) = (w − 3)² + λw². What is J(1) when λ = 2?

questions.stem: For which w is J(w) = (w − 4)² + w² smallest?
questions.explain: J′(w) = 2(w − 4) + 2w = 4w − 8, which is 0 at w = 2. Without the w² term the minimum would be at 4.

questions.stem: Least squares fits a line by minimising which quantity?
options: The number of points off the line
questions.explain: Ordinary least squares picks the line with the smallest total of squared residuals. Plain residuals would cancel out between positive and negative errors.

questions.stem: A matrix has rows (1, 2) and (3, 6). Which statement is true?
options: Its determinant is 12, so it has an inverse
Its determinant is 0, but it still has an inverse
Its determinant is 0, so it has no inverse
Its determinant is 3, so it has an inverse
questions.explain: The determinant is 1 × 6 − 2 × 3 = 0. A matrix with determinant 0 is singular and cannot be inverted.
